chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Wakes and funeral customs in Miami
summary: The body was brought home the night before the funeral; friends sang hymns, told stories and drank all night.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Now that you mentioned that, it reminded me -- that Sunday funeral business, was it similar to the New Orleans funerals?
It was the same thing. Like, you know, they used to have at the wake, they would have the wake set, and like if you died, all your friends would come by and different families would cook food.
Come by the day or night after you died?
No, they come by the night before the funeral, because they used to bring you home. They would bring the body home and have it in the living room, in a

corner of the house there, and all your friends would come in and -- say, they bring in the body at about five o'clock that evening, and they would start coming in around about five minutes after five, they would stop in and look at you, because they would have the casket open.

And they would sing hymns, they would talk about you and say, "Yeah, look at him laying up there -- remember the time he did such and such ..." and everybody would laugh about it, and they would tell different stories about him and they would drink and they would eat and go to sleep.
One crowd would go to sleep and another crew would come in -- and this went on all night long, until it was time for the funeral the next morning.
